description: Database of global regional, national, and platform regulatory deadlines compiled from App Store Compliance Playbook records.

deadlines.law: EU AI Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Article 4
deadlines.requirement: Article 4 AI literacy, as replaced on 27 July 2026. Providers and deployers take measures to support the development of AI literacy of their staff and other persons dealing with the operation and use of AI systems on their behalf, taking into account their technical knowledge, experience, education and training, the context the systems are used in, and the persons or groups on whom the systems are used. The obligation does not require guaranteeing any specific level of AI literacy of any individual. A written policy, induction, and log are pragmatic evidence, not a stated legal mandate.
deadlines.source_note: EUR-Lex HTML and PDF for CELEX 02024R1689-20260727 return a bot challenge. The consolidated Article 4 (Consolidated TEXT: 32024R1689, EN, 27.07.2026) was read on 19 November 2026 through the Publications Office CELLAR xhtml record http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/02024R1689-20260727.ENG (cellar:b1730fb2-8f1c-11f1-9262-01aa75ed71a1). It matches Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 Article 1(5), read the same day at http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj.
deadlines.history: 2026-11-19. Obligation narrowed in place. The 2 February 2025 application date is unchanged. Before Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 replaced Article 4, the entry required measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy.

deadlines.law: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA), 16 CFR Part 312
deadlines.requirement: Amended COPPA Rule compliance (biometric identifiers added to PII, separate opt-in consent for third-party disclosure/targeted-ads, written retention policy, written info-security program). The section 312.11 carve-outs are earlier dates (90 days and six months after the 22 April 2025 publication) and bind FTC-approved COPPA Safe Harbor programs only, not app developers.

deadlines.law: Texas SB 2420 (App Store Accountability Act)
deadlines.requirement: Age assurance and verifiable parental consent for minors on downloads, purchases, and major updates, delete age data, request age category. Statutory effective date 1 January 2026. Preliminary injunctions of 23 December 2025 were stayed by the Fifth Circuit on 4 June 2026 and the Supreme Court declined to vacate the stay on 6 July 2026, so the law is in force while the merits appeal is pending.
deadlines.source_note: Secondary comparison by the Future of Privacy Forum. The enrolled Texas bill was not read.

deadlines.law: Utah SB 142 (App Store Accountability Act) as amended by HB 498 (2026)
deadlines.requirement: Request and receive age category from store, confirm parental consent for minor accounts, delete verification data. HB 498 (2026) moved every substantive duty to Beginning May 6, 2027, brought pre-installed apps into scope, repealed Division rulemaking, and replaced AG enforcement with a private right of action (1,000 dollars per violation minimum). The CCIA challenge was voluntarily dismissed on 21 April 2026.

deadlines.law: Louisiana HB 977 (2026), Act No. 185, R.S. 51:1771 to 1775 (App Store Accountability Act), replacing HB 570 (2025)
deadlines.requirement: Age category request, parental consent, re-request consent on major updates. Act 481 of 2025 (HB 570) never takes effect. HB 977 re-enacts the regime effective 1 July 2027. Apple's storefront still exposes the Louisiana age-range signal on its own schedule.
deadlines.source_note: Secondary comparison by the Future of Privacy Forum. The enrolled Louisiana Act was not read.

deadlines.law: Alabama HB 161 (App Store Accountability Act)
deadlines.requirement: App stores verify age category, link minors to a parent account, and obtain verifiable parental consent per download and in-app purchase. Effective 1 January 2027 per HB 161 Section 14 (enrolled text). Accounts in existence on 2 October 2026 must be age-verified with consent before 1 October 2027.
deadlines.source_note: Secondary comparison by the Future of Privacy Forum. The enrolled Alabama bill was not read.

deadlines.law: Apple App Store Submission Requirements
deadlines.requirement: From 28 April 2026 apps uploaded to App Store Connect must be built with the iOS 26 and iPadOS 26 SDK or later (and the matching watchOS 26, tvOS 26, visionOS 26 SDKs). Apple states the requirement in SDK terms, not Xcode terms, and macOS is not in Apple's list. Age assurance features additionally require the iOS 26.2 SDK with Xcode 26.2 (17C52) or later.

deadlines.requirement: Starting April 2027 apps and games uploaded to App Store Connect must be built with the iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 SDK or later, and the matching tvOS 27, visionOS 27, and watchOS 27 SDKs. Apple has published the month only, no exact day, so this entry is tracked as 1 April 2027 and must be re-checked when Apple names the date. macOS is not in Apple's list. Announced 9 September 2026 with the Xcode 27 Release Candidate. Source https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=k1mtkt1k

deadlines.law: Google Play Billing Policy
deadlines.requirement: All new apps and updates must use Play Billing Library version 8 or later from 31 August 2026, with an extension available to 1 November 2026. This is a publishing gate, already-published v7 binaries keep transacting until the 2027 all-apps deadline.

deadlines.law: Google Play Target API Requirement
deadlines.requirement: New apps and updates must target API level 35 (Android 15) or higher, and existing target API 34+.

deadlines.law: Google Play Target API Requirement
deadlines.requirement: New apps and updates must target API level 36 (Android 16) or higher from 31 August 2026, with a Play Console extension request available to 1 November 2026. Wear OS and Android Automotive OS apps must target API 35 or higher, Android TV and Android XR apps API 34 or higher. Existing apps must target API 35 or higher to stay available to new users on newer devices.

Global expansion is stated only as 2027 with no exact date published. The separate Play leg (register every Play package name in Play Console by 30 September 2026, global) is GOOGLE-PLAY-APP-PACKAGE-REGISTRATION.

deadlines.law: Google Play chargeback cost responsibility update (Play Console Help answer 17068375)
deadlines.requirement: For orders placed after 3 August 2026 the developer bears the purchase price less the service fee plus the financial institution's chargeback fee. Google Play covers only its service fee. Handle PendingRefundReviewNotification and call the Review Refund API within 24 hours to contest illegitimate disputes.

deadlines.law: Play Console requirements. organization registration for financial, health, VPN, and government apps (Play Console Help answers 10788890 and 17125096)
deadlines.requirement: Apps offering financial products (banking, loans, stock trading, investment funds, crypto wallets and exchanges), health apps (medical, human subjects research), apps approved to use the VpnService class, and government apps must be published from an organization account with a D-U-N-S number consistent with the Dun and Bradstreet profile. Non-compliant apps are removed.

deadlines.law: Android developer verification, Play leg. register every Play app package name in Play Console (Play Console Help answers 17125096 and 17134731)
deadlines.requirement: Register your app package names via Play Console to comply with Android developer verification. This leg is global and separate from the Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand sideloading leg. Non-registration risks global removal from Google Play.

deadlines.law: US alternative billing and external links program. transaction reporting and service fees (Play Console Help answer 16497028)
deadlines.requirement: Developers enrolled in the US alternative billing or external links program must report transactions and successful downloads and pay the relevant Play service fee starting 1 October 2026.

deadlines.law: Play Catalog Access Program (Play Console Help answers 17117200 and 15582165)
deadlines.requirement: From 22 July 2026 registered third-party US Android app stores can access the Play catalog and list your app by default. Opt out in Play Console under Settings, Catalog Settings, if you do not want distribution through third-party stores.

deadlines.law: Contacts Permissions, Location Permissions, and Foreground Service policy changes for apps targeting Android 17, API level 37 (Play Console Help answers 16909972 and 16965181)
deadlines.requirement: Apps targeting API 37 or later may request READ_CONTACTS only when the Android Contact Picker is insufficient for core functionality (declaration required), must implement the Android location button with the onlyForLocationButton manifest flag for location-button scope, and may no longer use a foreground service for geofencing (use the Geofence API). Pre-review checks flag contacts and location issues in Play Console from 27 October 2026.

deadlines.law: Play Console technical quality requirements. memory, bitmap, and DEX optimization thresholds (Play Console Help answer 17492799)
deadlines.requirement: Google states From February 2027 (exact day not published) apps must meet minimum optimization of at least 25 percent coverage across optimization, shrinking, and obfuscation with a tool such as R8, must not hold bitmaps in memory in non-visible states, and must stay within memory bad-behavior thresholds. Failure affects visibility and publishing capabilities.

deadlines.law: Play Console technical quality requirements. Zero-Tap Sign-In restoration (Play Console Help answer 17492799)
deadlines.requirement: Google states From April 2027 (exact day not published) any app supporting user sign-in, optional or mandatory, must restore the user's sign-in state when they move to a new Android device using the Restore Credentials API. Games are currently out of scope.

deadlines.law: Age-Restricted Content, Families, and Child Safety Standards policy expansion to anonymous and random chat apps (Play Console Help answers 17036597, 17122218, 14747720)
deadlines.requirement: Apps whose core function is random or anonymous chat with strangers must use Play Console tools to block minors, may not target children under Families, and are in scope of the Child Safety Standards policy (published CSAE standards, in-app reporting, CSAM removal, child-safety contact).

deadlines.law: App Store Connect social media capability declaration (Apple Developer news 0d2gpmml and tlur8uvi)
deadlines.requirement: Apple states Starting September 2026 (no exact day published) you must indicate whether your app or game includes social media capabilities to submit a new version or update, or to notarize for alternative marketplaces. Declaring social media places the app in the Time Allowance category for Social Media with a minimum 13+ rating, and the Declared Age Range API is required to serve under-13 users.

From iOS 26.5 developers may distribute on alternative marketplaces, operate marketplaces, and process payments for digital goods outside Apple In-App Purchase in Brazil. deadlines.law: App Store regional age rating changes. Australia 15+ removed, Vietnam Decree 147 Article 38 region-specific rating (Apple Developer news yrrb45pw)

deadlines.law: Google Play Billing Library deprecation ladder (developer.android.com billing deprecation FAQ)

The 31 August 2026 v8 gate for new submissions carried an extension to 1 November 2026. Already-published lower-version binaries keep transacting until their deadline.

deadlines.law: ADA Title II web and mobile app accessibility, 28 CFR Part 35 Subpart H, Interim Final Rule FR Doc. 2026-07663 (20 April 2026)
deadlines.requirement: A mobile app provided or made available by a state or local government entity serving 50,000 or more people must conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA. Reaches a commercial developer through the contract or licensing chain. The 2024 date of 24 April 2026 was extended to 26 April 2027.

deadlines.law: ADA Title II web and mobile app accessibility, 28 CFR Part 35 Subpart H, Interim Final Rule FR Doc. 2026-07663
deadlines.requirement: Same WCAG 2.1 AA duty for public entities under 50,000 people and every special district government, extended to 26 April 2028.

deadlines.law: Section 504 web and mobile app accessibility for recipients of HHS financial assistance, 45 CFR 84.84(b), Interim Final Rule 91 FR 25496 (11 May 2026)
deadlines.requirement: A mobile app provided directly or through a contractual or licensing arrangement by any recipient of HHS federal financial assistance with 15 or more employees must conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA. Extended from 11 May 2026 to 11 May 2027.

deadlines.law: Section 504 web and mobile app accessibility, 45 CFR 84.84(b)(2), Interim Final Rule 91 FR 25496
deadlines.requirement: Same WCAG 2.1 AA duty for HHS-funded recipients with fewer than 15 employees, extended from 10 May 2027 to 10 May 2028.

deadlines.law: FTC Enforcement Policy Statement Promoting the Adoption of Age-Verification Technology under the COPPA Rule (25 February 2026)
deadlines.requirement: A general-audience or mixed-audience app may collect age data for age verification without COPPA enforcement risk only if it uses the data solely for age determination, minimises retention, vets third parties, notices parents and children, and secures the data. In force until final COPPA rule amendments are published or the statement is withdrawn.

deadlines.law: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 section 103 and Schedule 10, commenced by SI 2026/82 regulation 3
deadlines.requirement: Operate a data-protection complaints process. Acknowledge a data subject complaint within 30 days and respond without undue delay.

deadlines.law: ICO final Guidance on Storage and Access Technologies (29 April 2026), PECR regulation 6 with the DUAA Schedule A1 exemptions and the uplifted PECR penalty (17.5 million pounds or 4 percent of turnover)
deadlines.requirement: Re-audit every SDK, tracking pixel, and device-fingerprinting call against the guidance, not only cookies. A consent breach now carries the UK GDPR scale fine.

deadlines.law: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, Part 4 Chapter 2 subscription contracts regime
deadlines.requirement: Auto-renewing subscription apps sold to UK consumers need pre-contract information, renewal reminders, two cooling-off periods, an easy cancellation path, and the new refund rules. Government announced on 9 August 2026 that the regime commences in January 2027 (exact day not yet published), superseding the earlier spring 2027 estimate. The draft commencement instrument, The Consumer Subscription Contracts (Cancellation and Information) Regulations 2026, states 1 January 2027 but had not been made on 14 November 2026, so the day stays provisional until it is.

deadlines.law: Online Safety Act 2023, Ofcom statutory report on the use of app stores by children
deadlines.requirement: Ofcom publishes its report on app stores by January 2027. It feeds the Secretary of State decision on whether app stores are brought into scope of the Online Safety Act. Watch item, no direct developer duty yet.

deadlines.law: Under-16 social media ban and functionality restrictions, secondary legislation under the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Act (announced 15 June 2026)
deadlines.requirement: Regulations are to be laid before the end of 2026 and implemented in spring 2027 (exact day not yet published, tracked here as 1 March 2027). User-to-user social platforms must block under-16 accounts. For 16 and 17 year olds livestreaming and stranger contact are off by default, notifications are off from midnight to 6am, autoplay and personalised feeds are off by default. AI romantic companion chatbots must enforce a minimum age of 18.

deadlines.law: EU AI Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Article 111(4) and Article 5(1)(ba), (bb), (1a) and (1b)
deadlines.requirement: Article 111(4). Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, that generate synthetic audio, image, video or text and were placed on the market before 2 August 2026 take the necessary steps to comply with Article 50(2) by 2 December 2026. From the same date, Article 5(1a) prohibits placing on the market or putting into service an AI system that generates or manipulates non-consensual intimate material (Article 5(1)(ba)) or child sexual abuse material or performance (Article 5(1)(bb), Directive 2011/93/EU Article 2(c) and (e)) only where that generation or manipulation is the intended purpose, or where the system's design, training, architecture, capabilities or user-facing functionalities make it a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome without significant technical modification and the system lacks reasonable and adequate technical safety measures and other safeguards to reliably prevent it, taking into account reasonably foreseeable misuse, and to correct observed or reported misuse. Use is prohibited only where the deployer uses the system for that purpose. Article 5(1b): a manipulation that does not increase the exposure of any depicted intimate parts or alter the nature of any depicted sexually explicit activities is not manipulation under point (ba).
deadlines.source_note: EUR-Lex HTML and PDF for CELEX 02024R1689-20260727 return a bot challenge. The consolidated text (Consolidated TEXT: 32024R1689, EN, 27.07.2026) was read on 19 November 2026 through the Publications Office CELLAR xhtml record http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/02024R1689-20260727.ENG (cellar:b1730fb2-8f1c-11f1-9262-01aa75ed71a1). Article 111(4), Article 5(1)(ba), (bb), (1a) and (1b), and the Article 113 application date of 2 December 2026 match Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 Article 1(7), (39)(b) and (40)(a), read the same day at http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj.
deadlines.history: 2026-11-19. Requirement corrected in place. The 2 December 2026 date is unchanged. The previous text told operators to stop operating any AI system whose intended or reasonably foreseeable output is non-consensual intimate imagery or child sexual abuse material. Article 5(1a) limits placing on the market and putting into service to an intended purpose, or to a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome where safeguards and misuse correction are missing, and limits the use ban to a deployer who uses the system for that purpose.

deadlines.requirement: Name the CEO and representative as the final accountable parties, seat a board-approved chief privacy officer at qualifying scale, and absorb punitive surcharges plus widened breach notification.

deadlines.law: Personal Information Protection Act, Act No. 21445 (10 March 2026), Article 32-2(1) proviso and Article 75(2)(15)
deadlines.requirement: From 1 July 2027 a personal information handler that meets the threshold set by Presidential Decree, by revenue and the scale of personal information processed, must hold the Personal Information Protection Commission's privacy certification, and failing to obtain it carries an administrative fine. The decree threshold had not been published on 14 November 2026, so check whether your Korean operation falls under it once it is.

deadlines.law: Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act 2025, partial commencement
deadlines.requirement: Act on notice from the Online Safety Commission as a platform to address the five priority harms. Further harm categories follow progressively with no published date.

deadlines.law: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules 2025, G.S.R. 846(E), rule 4
deadlines.requirement: Registered Consent Managers commence one year after Gazette publication (13 November 2025). Be ready to interoperate with a registered Consent Manager ahead of the 18-month tranche on 13 May 2027.

deadlines.law: Act on the Protection of Personal Information amendment, promulgated 17 July 2026 (Act No. 56 of 2026, number from secondary sources), Act No. 56 of 2026 (令和8年法律第56号)
deadlines.requirement: Rebuild consent, children's data, and biometric handling for the amended APPI, including a new under-16 threshold where the legal representative is the party for consent, notice, and use-stop requests, plus a surcharge regime. Effective within two years of promulgation, exact day set by cabinet order. The amended penal provisions (Articles 176 and 178 to 186) apply from the day six months after promulgation under Supplementary Provisions Article 1 item 3, which is 17 January 2027 by calculation since the law states no calendar day. The surcharge regime waits for a Cabinet Order within two years of promulgation.

deadlines.requirement: Covered social media platforms display the Surgeon General black-box warning daily on first use, again after three cumulative hours, then hourly. Operative 1 January 2027.

deadlines.requirement: Companion chatbot operators report annually to the Office of Suicide Prevention on crisis referrals and protocols from 1 July 2027, on top of the disclosure and minor-protection duties already in force.

Apps built with Xcode 26 or earlier still run but do not extend under the status bar and camera. Build with Xcode 27.1 (beta from 18 September 2026) and the iOS 27.1 SDK, test every pose in the Duo simulator, resize from size classes and scene bounds, handle reserved regions (outer camera, inner camera when active, the folding region), and let navigation bars, toolbars, and tab bars present vertically. Since 5 October 2026 App Store Connect accepts iPhone Duo optimized apps and Duo screenshots, which earn a product page badge, and from April 2027 Duo screenshots are required for apps using the iOS 27.1 SDK or later (APPLE-IPHONE-DUO-SCREENSHOTS-REQ). Tracked in issue #724. Sources https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=kkphp5qo https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/09/apple-unveils-iphone-duo/ https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technologyoverviews/preparing-your-app-for-iphone-duo

deadlines.law: Personal Information Protection Act, Act No. 21910 (8 September 2026)
deadlines.requirement: From 9 March 2027 personal information collected lawfully for another purpose may be reused to develop AI technology when anonymous or pseudonymous processing would make that development difficult, the use serves a public interest or similar purpose, every statutory requirement is met, and the Personal Information Protection Commission deliberates and resolves on it. The handler must first run a risk-factor assessment of the impact on data subjects. An app that trains or tunes models on Korean user data plans the assessment before relying on this route.

deadlines.law: App Store Connect release notes, 12 November 2026
deadlines.requirement: Starting in early 2027, App Store Connect will no longer accept uploads containing On-Demand Resources from new apps or apps that have never used this feature. Migrating to Background Assets is recommended. Apple has published no exact day, so 1 January 2027 is the earliest possible date, kept only as a reminder to migrate early. It is not Apple's enforcement date. From that day the deadline checker lists it as passed, which is the intended prompt to confirm the real date, and the entry must be replaced when Apple names one. Apps that already use On-Demand Resources are not named in the block.

deadlines.law: Play Console trader status declaration under EEA and UK law (Play Console Help answer 17594752)
deadlines.requirement: Every active developer account must declare trader or non-trader status under EEA and UK law in Play Console, regardless of where its apps are targeted or distributed. An account that does not distribute in the EEA or the UK may declare non-trader. New accounts declare on creation. Existing accounts must declare by 1 February 2027. A trader self-certifies compliance with applicable laws, provides each app's terms of service link, and on a personal account provides a contact phone number (the address is displayed). Missing the date may block updates and remove the app from Play globally. A false non-trader declaration may result in global removal, and misrepresenting status to bypass verification or self-certification may suspend or terminate the account globally.
deadlines.source_note: Read on Play Console Help answer 17594752 on 19 November 2026. The 29 October 2026 policy announcement (answer 18100766) links to that page and says only that trader status must be declared in Play Console starting in November 2026. It publishes no day in November and does not state 1 February 2027, so effective_date is the announcement date, not a guessed 1 November. New accounts have no grace: the trader page says they declare immediately on creation. This is not GOOGLE-TECH-QUALITY-FEB-2027 and not EU-DSA-TRADER-STATUS.

deadlines.law: Play Console online marketplace model and trader information display for the EEA and the UK (Play Console Help answer 17594752)
deadlines.requirement: From 1 March 2027 Google Play uses an online marketplace model in the EEA and the UK. From that date, where the account has declared as a trader, users everywhere see the trader's contact details (a phone number and address for an individual account), the D-U-N-S number in App support, and a Terms of Service link when one was provided. Users in the EEA and the UK also see the developer or trader name in place of Google in the Offered by field, and the self-certification that products or services comply with local laws.
deadlines.source_note: Read on Play Console Help answer 17594752 on 19 November 2026. The 29 October 2026 policy announcement does not state 1 March 2027. This is the date the store starts displaying trader information, not a second declaration deadline. Existing accounts declare by the date in GOOGLE-PLAY-TRADER-STATUS-2027.

deadlines.law: App Store Connect China mainland compliance declarations (AI-Generated or Synthetic Content, and Security Assessment)
deadlines.requirement: Every app available on the App Store in China mainland must complete both declarations on the App Compliance page (Apps, then the app, then General in the sidebar). The required role is Account Holder or Admin. Select Yes if the app offers the feature to users in China mainland. Select No if it does not, or if the feature is disabled or geoblocked in China mainland. AI-Generated or Synthetic Content applies to services such as AI chatbots, image or video generation, and voice and face alteration. A Yes answer needs the approved filing number and registered filing name for the large language model or the algorithm. If those features are powered by someone else's technology, also upload an authorization or usage agreement from the technology owner that includes the registered name and filing number of the foundation model or algorithm, the provider name identifying you or your organization as the authorized party, and an authorizing entity whose name matches the owner on the Cyberspace Administration of China approval registry. Security Assessment applies to features such as distributing AI-generated or synthetic content or enabling end-to-end encrypted instant messaging. A Yes answer needs a screenshot from the National Internet Security Management Service Platform showing the app name, the provider name, and a status of pass or passed review, plus a copy of the Security Assessment report that includes the app name, the provider name, and the official company seal or chop. Redact confidential or proprietary information. Statuses are Missing Info, Pending Verification, Verification Failed, and Active. The app is released in every other selected country and region, and it is not available on the App Store in China mainland until the compliance information is verified. If the version is approved but verification fails, it stays unavailable in China mainland. Update and save the App Compliance page. The updated declarations are reviewed when the next app version is submitted. Once verified and approved, the app becomes available in China mainland. By 31 January 2027 every existing app in China mainland must have completed and verified compliance declarations to remain available on the App Store.
